summary.name: Cubox
summary.one_liner: Cubox is an AI read-later app and web clipper for saving web pages, articles and email newsletters, reading them cleanly, and annotating them.
use_cases: sync reading notes to Notion or Obsidian
read newsletters and WeChat articles on commute
summary.what_it_does: Cubox saves web pages, articles and email newsletters via a browser extension, mobile share sheet or email, and stores them in one reading space. It offers article parsing, automatic archiving of original pages, a distraction-free reader with highlights and notes, and AI features such as quick summaries, Q&A over saved content and voice reading. Users can organize items with nested folders and tags, and search full text and semantically. The page says saved content can be synced across supported clients under one account, and exported or pushed to note tools via sync, plugins or sharing.
notable: Browser extension, mobile share and email intake into one reading space
AI summaries, Q&A and text-to-speech on saved content
Cubox CLI and open API so AI agents can save and search the library
Automatic archiving of original web pages and export of data
caveats: Feature support varies by client and platform; the page defers to what each platform actually offers
Page text says one 14-day Pro+AI free trial per account; subscriptions started via app stores follow that platform's renewal and cancellation rules
Web-page parsing and archiving depend on the source site
Some features (HarmonyOS version, AI full-text translation, book highlight import) are planned or in development
